$comment: Bundle boundaries (design/12 'Bundle boundaries', design/04 WeChat package limits).
This file is the ONE place a shipped asset's package membership is decided, and it is
read by three consumers on purpose: the TypeScript runtime (render/assetManifest.ts,
which rewrites a path into its packed location), plain Node in the build
(build/wechatAssetSync.mjs), and the byte gate (build/checkWeChatPackage.mjs). A JSON
file is the only shape all three can read without a build step, which is what keeps
them from drifting apart.
WeChat's real limits (official 分包 docs, re-checked 2026-08-25): main package <= 4 MB,
a standard subpackage has NO individual cap, an INDEPENDENT subpackage <= 4 MB, and the
whole game (main + every subpackage) <= 30 MB. design/ROADMAP's parked note recorded only
the 4 MB main-package figure, which made the situation look more constrained than it is.
WHAT IS DEFERRED, AND WHY THESE AND NOTHING ELSE. Every subpackage below holds art that
is unreachable in a fresh run, checked against the shipped content rather than assumed:
- biome-ice / biome-lightning / biome-poison: theme.ts's BIOME_ID_TO_ELEMENT maps the
only authored dungeon ('ember') to 'fire', and everything without a dungeonConfig
(PvP, arena) falls to 'neutral'. So fire and neutral must stay in main and the other
three elements cannot be reached at all today.
- boss: 'blightlord' is the only user of skins/boss-core, and it spawns on floor 5 only.
- music: the two shipped loops (design/11 'Music & ambience', 2026-08-31). This one is
NOT justified by unreachability -- `menu` is wanted on the very first screen. It is
justified by bytes: 1.09 MB of audio in main takes the FIRST download from 4.00 to
5.09 MB, over the hard limit, and music is the one asset class a game can start
without. Nothing in the client reads these files yet, so today the pack is declared
and its contents are inert; when a player lands it should fetch this pack
fire-and-forget at boot -- the same non-blocking shape as `audio.preload()` -- rather
than awaiting it.
Explicitly NOT deferred: brute-core and floater-core. `brute` and `floater` both spawn on
FLOOR 1 (world/dungeons/ember/ember_l1_floor_1.json), so a pack holding them would be a
lie the moment anyone made it lazy.
HOW THEY LOAD TODAY: all of them, once, at boot (render/packLoader.ts, called from
preloadCoreArt). That satisfies WeChat's 4 MB main-package rule — which is a rule about
the FIRST download, not about total bytes — without paying for a per-room await. Making
a pack genuinely lazy later is an `ensurePack(name)` at the point of use plus dropping it
from the boot set; no loader and no manifest entry changes.
A rule matches by path PREFIX against the public-relative path a loader asks for (the
leading-slash form, e.g. '/biome/floor_ice.png'). First matching rule wins; anything
unmatched falls to `defaultPack`.
`limitBytes` on a subpackage is OUR guard, not WeChat's — a standard subpackage has no
individual cap, so this is only here to make a pack that quietly becomes the new dumping
ground fail the gate instead of the 30 MB total.

packs.name: main
packs.note: Boot-critical and WeChat's real 4 MB ceiling: every rig a floor-1 run can meet, the UI chrome, environment fixtures, weapons, and the fire/neutral biome swatches. Must also cover js/game.js.

packs.note: No authored dungeon maps to 'ice' yet (theme.ts BIOME_ID_TO_ELEMENT).
